title: Old Ironsides

evidence.note: Released in the US on 6 December 1926 by Paramount. Works published in 1926 passed out of US copyright by term on 1 January 2022 (95-year term).
evidence.source: Duke Center for the Study of the Public Domain, Public Domain Day 2022

evidence.note: The film is silent. The 1926 theatrical score (credited to Hugo Riesenfeld and J. S. Zamecnik) was published in 1926, but any score on a modern copy is a separate recording or arrangement and may be protected. I did not check the rights status of any specific score.

I could not confirm from a fetched page what source material the screenplay drew on. The one tie-in I found is the novelization 'Sons of the Sea' by A.M.R. Wright, published for the film's English release. I did not establish its date or status.

MoMA exhibited a restored 35mm print in December 2008. A faithful restoration adds no new US copyright, but any new score, titles or added material in a restored edition could be protected. I did not confirm the contents of that restoration.

watch.label: Old Ironsides (1926), dir. James Cruze, Internet Archive (about 115 min, listed as 1080p)

editorial:
Old Ironsides is a Paramount silent epic directed by James Cruze. It dramatizes the USS Constitution and the young US Navy's fight against the Barbary pirates. It premiered at New York's Rialto Theater on 6 December 1926. It used Paramount's Magnascope process to enlarge the screen image for selected sequences. For a creator it offers period naval spectacle, full-length and from the silent era, and the Internet Archive hosts a roughly 115-minute copy.

The film's 1926 publication means the picture itself is free in the US by term, and no renewal search is needed. The trap is everything attached to a particular copy. Any score on a modern copy is a separate recording or arrangement, and the original theatrical score is credited to Hugo Riesenfeld and J. S. Zamecnik. MoMA has shown a restored 35mm print, and a restored edition may add new titles or music. Take the images from a source whose soundtrack and added material you have cleared. I could not confirm what the screenplay was based on, so the story layer stays open.
faq: Can I reuse footage from Old Ironsides in my own video?

Yes for the images. The film was published in 1926, so the print is out of US copyright by term. Check each source copy for a modern score, new title cards or added material. Those additions can be protected even though the film is not.
Is the music on a modern copy free to use?

Not automatically. The film is silent, and the original 1926 score is credited to Hugo Riesenfeld and J. S. Zamecnik. A score on a modern release is a separate recording or arrangement that may be protected. Use a copy with no score, or one whose music you have cleared.
